title: Choosing what an image crop keeps
summary: object-fit: cover crops an image to its frame; object-position decides which part survives.
explanation: The same placeholder picture sits in three tall, narrow frames. object-fit: cover scales it to fill each frame and crops the sides, because the picture is wider than the frame.

object-position picks the anchor for that crop: left keeps the mountain's left slope, center the peak, right the sun. With real photos this keeps a face or product in view as the frame changes shape on different screens.
aspect-ratio gives each frame its shape from its width, so the crop stays the same as the column resizes.
tryThis: Change .frame's aspect-ratio to 16 / 9: the frames are now wider than the picture, so it crops top and bottom instead.
Change the third frame's object-position to 90% 20%.
Remove object-fit: cover: the picture is squashed to fit and object-position no longer matters.
